reason: The sole cited evidence (E1) only defines configurational entropy for random solid solutions in different alloy systems; it provides no data on CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles, no evidence linking quenching/annealing to atomic order, and no support for the mechanistic claims about premelting or nucleation. All key premises thus lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Rapid quenching preserves a highly random atomic configuration in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Slow annealing promotes detectable short-range order (local clustering) in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid solution and delays premelting.
Local clustering creates lattice distortions that act as nucleation sites for premelting.
Differences in atomic order can be reliably quantified by TEM, synchrotron X-ray scattering, or APT.
